prior_coverage: Heavily swept before. Apify: store-promotion, agent-markets, productized-services and distribution audits on 3.9, then the 7.9 board. The line `apify-actors` is committed at ₪200 as a ₪0 instrument (REJECTED.md:1293, BOARD.md:99). A second Actor is gated at 50 stranger users and pricing at 200 (BOARD.md:86, BOARD.md:328). The niche is occupied by parseforge, bovi, lentic_clockss (33 sources) and swerve (REJECTED.md:343-351, 455-474; audits/agent-markets.md:97-109). Splitting the generic CKAN Actor into per-dataset listings was judged substitution (audits/agent-markets.md:232-247). Ranking rests on prior success (REJECTED.md:1113). RapidAPI: scout agent-markets--rapidapi.md (3.9) put it at ₪0-800. The store-promotion audit cut it to ₪500, with ₪0 for 90 days (REJECTED.md:324-326). The paid-apis line died on 7.9 (REJECTED.md:1221-1228). n8n, Zapier, Make and HubSpot were covered in scouts/distribution--partnerships-integrations.md:31-62 (4.9): n8n had no creator payment, Zapier needs 50 users, Make needs a partnership agreement. Hugging Face and Replicate were covered in scouts/agent-markets--inference-hosting.md:84-100 (3.9): no creator payout. MCP registries, Smithery and x402 are rejected (REJECTED.md:281-282; INCOME_PLAN.he.md:267). New this sweep: API-driven Apify publishing (github); statistics computed from the already-rendered Apify Store capture (815 Actors); n8n paid templates with a purchaseUrl (snippet) and in-product template discovery (github); MCPize and AgenticMarket (snippet). Pipedream, Postman and Val Town were never covered, and no evidence of creator payouts was found for them (grade none).

candidates.venue: Apify Store: a fleet of distinct-source pay-per-event Actors on one brand account
candidates.what_we_would_list: The one Actor already built (data.gov.il CKAN wrapper) plus 6-10 net-new Actors, each on a genuinely distinct Israeli public source or job. Candidates: Knesset OData (bills, votes, committee sessions, MKs); Bank of Israel SDMX series; CBS series and CPI indexation; Israel Land Authority tenders; the Ministry of Health drug registry; gov.il dynamic-collector publications and decisions; election results; a vehicle-by-plate join across the data.gov.il MOT resources; bulk validation of Israeli ID (ת״ז) checksums, phone numbers and bank/branch formats, reusing products/x402-il-api/src/israeli.ts. Left out because they are occupied: supermarket prices (swerve, plus a free daily Kaggle dump), the companies registrar (parseforge, bovi) and real estate (alinz). The honest count is therefore about 7-11 Actors, one per distinct source (growth.ts:279 STORES_PER_DISTINCT_DATASET=1; checkHonestStorePlan growth.ts:301). Each listing states that its source is free (BOARD.md:316) and links nowhere off-platform (Store terms §2.2.4.2(i)).
candidates.existing_product: products/apify-il-open-data: built and tested, unpublished. It waits on owner step 6a (logs/CHANNEL_LOOP.md:106).
candidates.listings_per_owner_step: One Apify account (step 6a) covers unlimited Actors. Each extra listing costs zero owner clicks, because publishing is an API call (see the programmatic gate). One more one-time step, KYC with an ID photo plus PayPal or Wise, unlocks pricing and payout for every Actor at once.
candidates.prior_verdict: ALIVE but capped. `apify-actors` is committed at ₪200, with ₪1,500 as a contested upper bound (REJECTED.md:1293; INCOME_PLAN.he.md:247 'first payment estimated at month 9'). A second Actor, KYC and pricing are gated at 50/50/200 stranger users in 30 days (BOARD.md:328). The niche is occupied (REJECTED.md:343-351, 463-474). Per-dataset splitting was ruled substitution (audits/agent-markets.md:232-247). Maintenance is about 2 h per week per Actor (portfolio.ts:63-65).
candidates.reopen_basis: There is no evidence that the occupancy finding is false. The 28.9 breadth directive changes which plan shape is preferred, not the evidence. Three new facts bear on the fleet question, and the board (Fable) should rule on them. (1) github: publishing needs no Console click. apify-api/openapi/paths/actors/acts@{actorId}.yaml says: 'To make your Actor public: Set `isPublic` to `true`. Provide `title` and `categories`.' UpdateActorRequest.yaml also carries `pricingInfos`. So PUBLISH.md:39 and README.md:150 overstate the owner's work, and N free listings cost the owner nothing beyond step 6a. (2) rendered: fleet creators in the stored Store capture get users. unseenuser has 37 Actors at a median of 24 users per 30 days; memo23 has 24 at 20.5; automation-lab has 22 at 6; gio21 has 13 at 1. (3) snippet: Apify's own post says '$1M paid to creators in a single month. A year ago: $222K.' The case to put to the board is to publish the 6-10 distinct-source Actors free in parallel as one wider measurement (N=8 instead of N=1). The per-Actor pricing and KYC gates would stay as ruled.

gate_zero_cost.evidence: Store Publishing Terms (raw apify-docs, fetched this session). No direct fees. Apify keeps 20% of user fees, and platform usage costs are deducted from fees (§10.2.1), so the cost comes out of sales. The account is free and a free Actor needs no payment (PUBLISH.md). Risks: a negative-profit Actor has its payout zeroed for the month (portfolio.ts:77); our own test runs must stay inside the free plan's monthly credit.

gate_israel_payout_no_camera.evidence: monthly-payouts.mdx (raw apify-docs). An individual's KYC is 'Provide the full name that matches your legal ID card' and 'Upload a clear, high-resolution photo of your ID card or driver's license'. No selfie, liveness check or video is named, and the verification provider is not named. Payout is PayPal or Wise at a $20 minimum, other methods at $100, invoiced on the 11th. The Store terms name no excluded country (audits/agent-markets.md:250-253). Open: whether the provider triggers a liveness check, and whether the legal name shows on the Verified Creator profile (audits/agent-markets.md:408-413). Both are confirmed only at KYC, which is needed only for pricing.

gate_programmatic_listing.evidence: The Apify API's Update Actor operation publishes to the Store with isPublic=true plus title and categories. The schema also carries pricingInfos. `apify push` from CI creates and builds the Actor (.github/workflows/apify-publish.yml). The whole create-build-publish cycle is API-driven, with no per-item owner click.

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: The Store Publishing Terms contain no clause about AI-generated or automated content. They forbid copying another creator's code or README (§2.2.3), off-platform promotion (§2.2.4.2(i)) and fake or incentivised reviews (§2.2.4.2), and Apify may unpublish at its discretion (§2.2.4.3). The $1M Challenge terms disqualify 'too many low-quality or spammy Actors' (audits/agent-markets.md:238-240), so the fleet must stay at one Actor per distinct source.

gate_buyer_supply.evidence: research/rendered/apify-store-accessibility.json (api.apify.com/v2/store?search=accessibility, captured 2026-09-22): 815 of 1,499 results. 798 are PAY_PER_EVENT. Median users in 30 days is 2; 695 Actors have at least 1 user, 200 have at least 10, 87 have at least 50. 674 are whitelisted for agentic payments. Snippet: Apify reports $1M paid to creators in one month, up 5x in a year (x.com/apify/status/2054547299485745273). The capture is a search sample, not a random one, and it has no Actor creation date, so cold start cannot be isolated from it.

candidates.discovery_needs_prior_sale: No sale is needed, but Store ranking correlates with a quality score whose Popularity and History-of-success categories cannot move on day one (REJECTED.md:308-315, 800-802; audits/agent-markets.md:77-80). A new Actor is disadvantaged, not invisible: in the rendered sample 85% of pay-per-event Actors had at least one user in 30 days. Actors also reach agents through Apify's MCP search-actors tool, but agentic payments require the developer's KYC (_agentic-payments-eligibility.mdx).
candidates.owner_step: Step 6a, already on the checklist: Apify sign-up with the brand username and APIFY_TOKEN as a GitHub secret. The per-Actor 'Publish to Store' click can be dropped, since CI can call the API. Later, and only when the board's stranger-user gate fires: KYC with an ID photo and PayPal or Wise details, once for all Actors.
candidates.estimate_basis: INFERENCE. Low: ₪0 if no stranger finds the Israeli niche (constraint 7; the competitors' user counts have not been rendered). High: 8 priced Actors × 2-8 users per month (rendered median 2; the board's base rate is 8.7 users per Actor, audits/agent-markets.md:186) × $1-4 per user per month × 80%, minus platform usage (data.gov.il needs no proxy, so usage is low) ≈ $15-200 per month, plus one breakout Actor, is about ₪900 at most. Net of the PayPal-fee VAT (18%) and 5-9% FX drag. It rests on pricing being allowed, which today requires 200 stranger users (BOARD.md:328).
candidates.time_to_first_sale: Listed free on day 0 after step 6a; stranger usage is readable within 30 days. Pricing needs KYC plus the board gate, and a price change takes effect after 14 days (§9.4). The first $20 PayPal payout is invoiced on the 11th. A realistic first ledger entry is month 3 at best and month 9 by the prior audit (audits/agent-markets.md:198-200). A balance under $20 is forfeited after 12 months (§10.3.2).

gate_ai_allowed_honest.evidence: The scout rated the ToS GREEN: listing your own API is the intended use (agent-markets--rapidapi.md F1). No AI clause was found. Honesty caveat: the endpoints are thin wrappers over free logic and data.
